standard_prerequisites.name: For a perfect complex K_n with dual K_n^dual = RHom(K_n, A) one has E tensor K_n^dual = RHom_A(K_n, E) for every E
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the right-hand side into a limit of Hom complexes.

standard_prerequisites.name: The derived colimit of a system is the cone of the canonical map from the direct sum to itself
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies K with the cone of a map of direct sums, matching the Rlim triangle.

standard_prerequisites.name: The internal-hom adjunction formula Hom(K, RHom(L, M)) = Hom(K tensor L, M)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces Hom out of a direct sum to a product of Hom complexes.

core_obligations: By the dual-perfect-complex lemma, E tensor K_n^dual = RHom_A(K_n, E), and these fit into the distinguished triangle Rlim RHom(K_n, E) -> prod RHom(K_n, E) -> prod RHom(K_n, E) computing the derived limit (proof lines 19251-19259). The hocolim K_n sits in the analogous triangle with direct sums in place of products, so both sides of the claimed equality have the same cohomology provided prod RHom_A(K_n, E) = RHom_A(hocolim-free direct sum, E); by the internal-hom formula this Hom out of a direct sum is the product of the Hom complexes, and the identification uses that derived tensor product commutes with direct sums (proof lines 19260-19264).
proof_roadmap: Rewrite the dual system via the dual-perfect-complex lemma and the Rlim triangle (proof lines 19251-19259).
Match with the hocolim triangle and reduce to the internal-hom adjunction (proof lines 19260-19264).
